chunks: Know then, therefore, there is no god but He, and ask forgiveness for your sins and those of believing men and women. God knows your wanderings and your destination.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of seeking forgiveness for both oneself and other believers in this verse?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often cited to establish the necessity of intercessory forgiveness, where the Prophet seeks pardon not only for himself but collectively for the community of believers. It underscores the divine attribute of 'Alim' (All-Knowing) regarding both the transient actions ('mutaqallabikum') and the ultimate abode ('mathwakum') of the faithful, reinforcing the link between belief, repentance, and divine surveillance.
